title: de.hubtask.work.item.moved.v1
description: An item sits somewhere else: under a different parent, in a different collection, or at a different rank among the same siblings. One event for all three, because domain-model.md §4 gives movement one event and names `orderKey` among its payload - a drag within a list and a drag between lists are the same gesture to a person and the same event to a rule. A consumer that cares only about reparenting compares `from_parent_id` with `to_parent_id`; one that cares only about order reads `order_key`. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: The item as it now stands, in the field names of the API (schema WorkItem), plus where it came from. The "from" half cannot be read off the snapshot, which is the new state; the "to" half is the snapshot, so it is not repeated except as to_parent_id, which domain-model.md §4 names.

type.description: The level. Extensible by configuration: a consumer that switches on it must tolerate a value it does not know rather than fail (domain-model.md §1).

collection_id.description: The collection the item belongs to. Sent on every level, because the parent alone does not say which collection an item is in until the whole chain has been walked.

parent_id.description: The item above; null for one that sits directly under the collection (invariant I-W1). Sent even when null - it is the parent reference a consumer places the item by, and inferring it from the type would break the day a level is added.

path.description: The materialised path, `/<id>/<id>/…/`, including the item itself and closed by a separator (invariant I-W2).

depth.description: The level below the collection, counting from 1. Bounded by the capability profile of the type.

notes.description: Markdown, unrendered by the server. Absent when unset, and absent on a type whose profile does not carry the NOTES capability.

completion.description: The done/open state. Always sent, though a created item is always open: a rule that reads it should not need a special case for the one event where it happens to be absent.

order_key.description: The rank among the siblings: a fractional index, not a number (offline-sync.md §4.2).

updated_at.description: When the item last changed - the instant of this move.

from_parent_id.description: The item it sat under before, null if it sat directly in a collection. Equal to to_parent_id when the move was a reorder within one level.

to_parent_id.description: The item it sits under now, null for the top level of a collection. The same value as parent_id in the snapshot, and named here because domain-model.md §4 names it.

from_path.description: The materialised path before the move. Together with `path` it is the prefix swap a client applies to its own copy of the subtree: every descendant's new path is its old one with from_path replaced by path. That is why a moved subtree needs no event per descendant (I-W2).

from_collection_id.description: The collection it was in before, set only when the move crossed collections. A device subscribed to one hub reads it to know the item has left its scope (offline-sync.md §3.1).

from_bucket_id.description: Reserved, always null on this version: buckets arrive with B-09. In the documented payload, so a kanban consumer can be written against the final shape.

to_bucket_id.description: Reserved, always null on this version. See from_bucket_id.
